title: Native sheaf open tensor and K-flat preservation
statement: Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and a $k_0$-open immersion $j:U\to Z$ between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes. Use the actual native pro-etale Weil-sheaf categories and open functors of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], the native tensor and categorical two-sided K-flatness of [def-sf-derived-weil-category-and-operations], and the data type of [def-sf-native-open-tensor-presentation-data]. There exist an extension/restriction adjunction whose unit and counit forget to the ordinary open adjunction, the generator-normalized equivariant sheaf restriction/tensor isomorphism, the equivariant sheaf open tensor isomorphism whose inverse is its specified unit transpose, and preservation of categorical two-sided K-flatness by extension and restriction. Invertibility of the lifted unit is not a conclusion here; it is deduced from the ordinary open unit by the assembling theorem. This statement concerns sheaves and complexes only; it asserts no ambient derived comparison or forgetting square.

source.place: Tag 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; Tags 03DJ, 03D8; native parent proof steps 1--4

proof.text: Use the actual module operations of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. The open is Frobenius-stable because it is defined over $k_0$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] its geometric pro-etale site is the slice at $U$; the localized coefficient sheaf is $B_U=j^{-1}B_Z$, since both assign the same locally finite functions to every slice object. [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] gives exact restriction and exact extension, with their specified adjunction. The ordinary open unit is invertible by [lem-sf-native-adic-open-restrictions]; reflection of this property is reserved for the assembling theorem. These maps lift to Weil sheaves: restriction sends a section to itself, the open unit sends $x$ to $[x]$, and the counit sends $[x]$ to $x$ on a factoring object. Frobenius reindexes the factoring object and applies its structure map to $x$, so these formulas commute with it. Thus the underlying adjunction bijection and its inverse restrict to commuting morphisms. [lem-sf-fixed-pair-created-abelian-structure] makes forgetting faithful, exact and conservative, so the lifted operations are exact ; the assembling theorem reflects the invertibility of the ordinary unit. This also shows that $j_{0!}$ reflects acyclicity: apply $j_0^*$ and its unit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-ringed-slice-tensor-generators] with $O=B_Z$. For Weil module sheaves $P,T$ the underlying forward map is $[x]_f\otimes y\mapsto[x\otimes y|_U]_f$ and its inverse is $[x\otimes z]_f\mapsto[x]_f\otimes z$. Here the inverse formula is interpreted locally on the slice, exactly as the cited sheaf-map assertion. These maps commute with the Weil structures specified in [def-sf-derived-weil-category-and-operations]: on a pulled-back generator the two orders both give $[\phi_P(F_U^*x)\otimes j^*\phi_T(F_Z^*y)]_{F(f)}$. The coefficient action commutes because restriction and Frobenius both act on functions by precomposition and $jF_U=F_Zj$. Faithfulness of forgetting from step 1 turns this equality on the defining generators into equality of Weil-sheaf maps. The two underlying inverse identities therefore give inverse Weil maps. The same formulas prove naturality in both module morphisms.

source.place: Tags 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact), 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules); native equivariant refinement by Q85

proof.text: Apply the maps of step 2 in every bidegree and take direct sums. [lem-sf-ringed-open-total-tensor-kflat] supplies the underlying natural chain isomorphism with precisely this direct-sum convention. Coproducts in the Weil category have their underlying coproducts by [lem-sf-fixed-pair-created-abelian-structure]. Therefore the bidegree maps of step 2 assemble to a Weil chain isomorphism $\Gamma_{P,T}:\operatorname{Tot}(j_{0!}P\otimes T)\cong j_{0!}\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes j_0^*T)$. Explicitly, the two composites with the differential send $[x]_f\otimes y$ in bidegree $(p,q)$ to $[d_Px\otimes y|_U]_f+(-1)^p[x\otimes(d_Ty)|_U]_f$. The inverse has the same bidegrees and signs. Naturality is inherited on every summand, so holds for arbitrary unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tags 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact), 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules); native equivariant refinement by Q85

proof.text: Check categorical K-flatness directly using the definition in [def-sf-derived-weil-category-and-operations]. If $P$ is K-flat on $U$ and $a:T\to T'$ is a quasi-isomorphism on $Z$, then $j_0^*a$ is a quasi-isomorphism by step 1. Step 3 identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(j_{0!}P\otimes a)$ with $j_{0!}\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes j_0^*a)$, hence it is a quasi-isomorphism. Conversely let $T$ be K-flat on $Z$ and $b:P\to P'$ a quasi-isomorphism on $U$. Step 3 identifies $j_{0!}\operatorname{Tot}(b\otimes j_0^*T)$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(j_{0!}b\otimes T)$, which is a quasi-isomorphism. Reflection of acyclicity by $j_{0!}$ from step 1 proves the same for $\operatorname{Tot}(b\otimes j_0^*T)$. Symmetry gives the other tensor variable. These arguments concern arbitrary categorical K-flat complexes, without a flat-term restriction.

lean.statement:
theorem native_open_sheaf_tensor_existence :
    ∃ (adj : extensionByZero k₀ l j ⊣ upperStar k₀ l j)
      (sheafRestriction : ∀ M N : ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l Z,
        (upperStar k₀ l j).obj (tensor k₀ l Z N M) ≅
          tensor k₀ l U ((upperStar k₀ l j).obj N) ((upperStar k₀ l j).obj M))
      (sheafGamma : ∀ (M : ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l U) (N : ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l Z),
        tensor k₀ l Z N ((extensionByZero k₀ l j).obj M) ≅
          (extensionByZero k₀ l j).obj (tensor k₀ l U ((upperStar k₀ l j).obj N) M)),
      (∀ M, (adj.unit.app M).hom.f =
        (ProEtale.adicOpenImmersionLowerShriekAdjunction l
          (Scheme.Hom.geometricFiberMap j (comp_over j _))).unit.app M.carrier) ∧
      (∀ N, (adj.counit.app N).hom.f =
        (ProEtale.adicOpenImmersionLowerShriekAdjunction l
          (Scheme.Hom.geometricFiberMap j (comp_over j _))).counit.app N.carrier) ∧
      (∀ M N, HEq ((sheafRestriction M N).hom.hom.f)
        ((ProEtale.adicUpperStarTensorLeftIso l
          (Scheme.Hom.geometricFiberMap j (comp_over j _)) N.carrier).hom.app M.carrier)) ∧
      (∀ M N, HEq (adj.homEquiv _ _ ((sheafGamma M N).inv))
        ((tensorFunctor k₀ l U ((upperStar k₀ l j).obj N)).map (adj.unit.app M) ≫
          (sheafRestriction ((extensionByZero k₀ l j).obj M) N).inv)) ∧
      (∀ P, NativeIsKFlat k₀ l U P → NativeIsKFlat k₀ l Z
        (((extensionByZero k₀ l j).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)) ∧
      (∀ T, NativeIsKFlat k₀ l Z T → NativeIsKFlat k₀ l U
        (((upperStar k₀ l j).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj T))
